titulo: I hope you have arrived safely
intro: The perfect subjunctive: «haya» plus the participle, for something that should already have happened.
p.haya.consejo: It always goes with a participle: «haya llegado». The h is silent: A-ya.
p.hayas.consejo: It is the tú form: «espero que hayas llegado». With the participle it forms the perfect subjunctive.
p.hayamos.consejo: It is the nosotros form: «ojalá hayamos acertado». The stress falls on «ya».
p.hayan.consejo: It is the form for ellos and ustedes: «no creo que hayan salido». The initial h is silent.
p.me extraña que.consejo: It expresses surprise and asks for the subjunctive: «me extraña que no haya llamado».
p.me alegro de que.consejo: It comes from «alegrarse de». After «que» the subjunctive follows: «me alegro de que hayas venido».
p.no creo que.consejo: The negation triggers the subjunctive: «no creo que haya llegado». Affirmative «creo que» takes the indicative.
p.gracias por haber venido.consejo: After «por» comes the compound infinitive, «haber venido». You can also say «gracias por venir».
p.vuelo.consejo: It is masculine and comes from «volar»: the o changes to «ue». It sounds BWE-lo.
p.mensaje.consejo: It is masculine: «un mensaje». The j sounds like h: men-SA-he.
p.descansar.consejo: A regular -ar verb. It is also used with «de»: «descansar de un viaje».
b1.titulo: Something that should already be done
b1.texto:
The **perfect subjunctive** is **haya** + participle. It says that something already happened before now:

- Ha llegado. → Espero que **haya llegado**.
- Has aprobado. → Me alegro de que **hayas aprobado**.
- No ha llamado. → Me extraña que no **haya llamado**.

Compare: espero que **llegues** bien (the journey has not finished yet) and espero que **hayas llegado** bien (it should be over by now).
b2.f0.texto: Do you know anything about Ana?
b2.f1.texto: It surprises me that she has not called.
b2.f2.texto: I do not think she has arrived yet.
b2.f3.texto: I hope she has not had any problems.
b2.f4.texto: A message from her has reached me.
b2.f5.texto: I am glad she has arrived safely.
b2.f6.texto: Tell her to call us when she has rested.
b2.f7.texto: Thank you for coming to wait with me.
b4.titulo: Forms of haber: haya, hayas, haya…
b4.texto:
The six forms of **haber** in the subjunctive are: **haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan**. A **participle** follows: haya llegado, hayas comido, hayan salido.

Irregular participles: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto.

You use it where the subjunctive is needed and the action is already done:

- Reactions: Me alegro de que **hayas venido**.
- Doubts: No creo que **haya salido**.
- Finished future time: Llámame cuando **hayas terminado**.

After **gracias por** the compound infinitive is used: gracias por **haber venido**.
b4.e0.texto: I hope you have arrived safely.
b4.e1.texto: I do not think they have left yet.
b4.e2.texto: Call me when you have finished.
b5.f0.texto: In the living room, the lamp draws a yellow circle on the rug.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía looks at her phone every five minutes with a silent hope.
b5.f2.texto: The night presses against the windowpanes like a dark hand.
b5.f3.texto: In the kitchen, the old clock counts the minutes in a low voice.
b5.f4.texto: Pablo pours two cups of tea and forgets them on the table.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly, the screen lights up with a blue tremor.
b5.f6.texto: Ana's message is short and says that she is fine.
b5.f7.texto: Lucía breathes deeply and smiles for the first time all night.
b5.f8.texto: On the roof, the first rain of autumn begins to fall.
b5.f9.texto: The friends listen to the murmur of the water in the half-light.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Ha» is indicative and «espero que» asks for the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Habría» is conditional: it does not work after «espero que».
b6.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Haya» plus participle expresses something already finished.
b6.pregunta: You want her to have arrived by now. Which form is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Llegues» looks forward: the trip has not ended yet.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Correct: «hayas llegado» says the trip should already be over.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Llegarás» is future indicative; after «espero que» the subjunctive is needed.
b7.pregunta: Which sentence speaks of a trip that has already ended?
b8.frase: Me alegro de que hayas llegado bien
b8.traduccion: I am glad you have arrived safely
b9.o0.refuerzo: Well done: «ellos» needs «hayan» and «no creo que» asks for the subjunctive.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Han» is indicative: it is not used after «no creo que».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Habrían» is conditional and changes the meaning of the sentence.
b9.pregunta: You doubt something others have done. Which form is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! In the future, «cuando» takes the subjunctive.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Has terminado» is indicative; here you speak of the future.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Habrás» is future and does not follow «cuando».
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I hope you have slept well.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Hayas» is subjunctive and needs «que»: «que hayas venido».
b12.o1.refuerzo: Exactly: after «por» comes the compound infinitive «haber venido».
b12.pregunta: After «por» comes a verb form. Which one?
p.llegado.consejo: Participle of «llegar». With «haya» it forms the perfect subjunctive: «haya llegado».
p.espero.consejo: From «esperar», for yo. «Espero que» asks for the subjunctive when the person changes.
p.tenido.consejo: Participle of «tener». With «haya» it forms «haya tenido». The accent falls on «NI».
p.llame.consejo: Present subjunctive of «llamar»: the a becomes e. In «dile que nos llame», someone else calls.
p.descansado.consejo: Participle of «descansar». With «haya» it forms «haya descansado». The accent falls on «SA».
p.terminado.consejo: Participle of «terminar». With «haya» it forms «cuando hayas terminado». The stress is on «NA».
p.esperanza.consejo: It is feminine: «la esperanza». The z sounds like th: es-pe-RAN-tha. It comes from «esperar».
p.callada.consejo: Feminine of «callado». It comes from «callar», to be silent. The ll sounds like y.
p.aprieta.consejo: From «apretar»: the e becomes «ie» in the singular: «aprieta». The «ie» sounds as one beat.
p.cristales.consejo: Plural of «cristal». It ends in -l, so the stress is at the end; the plural keeps it: kris-TA-les.
p.tazas.consejo: Plural of «taza». The z becomes c before e only: «tazas» keeps the z. It sounds TA-thas.
p.olvida.consejo: From «olvidar». The v sounds like b: ol-BI-da. It is the opposite of «recordar».
p.enciende.consejo: From «encender»: the e becomes «ie» in the singular. The c sounds like th: en-THYEN-de.
p.temblor.consejo: It is masculine: «un temblor». It comes from «temblar» and ends in -r, so the stress is at the end.
p.breve.consejo: The same for masculine and feminine: «un mensaje breve», «una carta breve». The v sounds like b.
p.tejado.consejo: It is masculine: «el tejado». The j sounds like h. It comes from «teja», a roof tile.
p.otoño.consejo: It is masculine: «el otoño». The ñ sounds like ny: o-TO-nyo. Seasons are written in lowercase.
p.penumbra.consejo: It is feminine: «la penumbra». The «mb» is pronounced m-b: pe-NUM-bra. It comes before real darkness.
p.haber.consejo: Auxiliary verb of the compound tenses: «haber» + participle. The h is silent and the b sounds like v.
